text: "The database is slow" is almost never precise enough to act on. Before you touch a single index or execution plan, this chapter starts with the decision tree for what to check first, and in what order.

Three questions, in order. Is this one query or the whole system -- those have almost entirely different fixes. Is it new, a regression, or has it always been this slow. And only then do you check what SQL Server is actually waiting on.

sys.dm_os_wait_stats tells you, instance-wide, what SQL Server has spent the most cumulative time waiting on. A page I/O latch wait means disk, not a missing index. A lock wait means blocking -- Lesson 50's topic, not an execution plan problem.

A crib sheet you'll use constantly: PAGEIOLATCH points to disk I/O, LCK_M points to blocking and locking, CXPACKET/CXCONSUMER points to parallelism, SOS_SCHEDULER_YIELD points to CPU pressure. The wait type tells you which tool applies.
Scope it, time it, check waits first, then reach for a specific tool. Next up: reading a real graphical execution plan, and what its arrows and percentages are actually telling you.
